cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ (James 1:1), is writing to believers he calls his brothers. He's just finished warning rich people who held back the wages of their workers (James 5:4). Now he turns back to the brothers and tells them to be patient until the Lord's coming.

cards.question: James wants to give the brothers a picture of patience they can see. Who does he point to?
The farmer in James's picture is waiting on the precious fruit of the soil. He's patient for the fall and spring ___.

cards.text: Then James turns it right back to the brothers: you, too, be patient. That farmer can't hurry the rain any more than I can hurry my oven timer, and friend, I have BEGGED that timer.

cards.question: True or false: James tells the brothers to be patient and strengthen their hearts, because the Lord's coming is near.

cards.text: No date from James, and Jesus said only the Father knows the day (Matthew 24:36), so my job is simple: keep the ovens ready. Meanwhile, James has a warning about how the brothers treat one another.

cards.question: While the brothers wait, what does James tell them not to do to one another?
James tells the brothers not to complain about each other, so they won't be judged. Then he tells them to look, because the ___ is standing at the door.

cards.text: Griping about a coworker when the boss is standing in the doorway is bad enough, but with the Judge at the door, my mustache slaps over my mouth SO fast. Then James gives the brothers an example of patience in affliction.

cards.question: True or false: As an example of patience in affliction, James points the brothers to the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

cards.text: James says we consider those who have persevered blessed. Then he names one man the brothers have heard about, a man who lost his flocks, his herds and his children (Job 1:13-19).

cards.question: Which man's perseverance does James remind the brothers about?

cards.text: James reminds them they've seen the outcome the Lord brought for Job. Honestly, I did years in a junk drawer and thought I had it rough, but Job makes my drawer look like a vacation.

cards.question: After bringing up Job, what does James say about the Lord?

answers.text: He is full of compassion and mercy
He tests those who love Him

cards.text: Then James says, "Above all, my brothers," and turns to the way they talk.

cards.question: Above all, James tells the brothers, do not ___, not by heaven or earth.
True or false: James says a plain yes or no isn't enough without an oath.

cards.text: Next, James goes mood by mood. Is anyone suffering? He should pray.

cards.question: And if one of the brothers is cheerful, what does James say he should do?

cards.text: Next on James's list: anyone who's sick. And friend, his answer is NOT looking up your symptoms at 2 a.m.

cards.question: James says anyone who is sick should call the ___ of the church.
True or false: James says the elders should pray over the sick person and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
What does James say the prayer offered in faith will do for the one who is sick?

answers.text: It will show him his sin

cards.question: James says the Lord will raise the sick one up. And if he has sinned, he will be ___.

cards.text: So James tells the brothers to confess their sins to each other and pray for each other, so that they may be healed.

cards.question: True or false: James says only the prayer of a prophet has great power to prevail.

cards.text: Then James brings up Elijah, a prophet in Israel (1 Kings 18:36), and says he was a man just like us. Well, just like YOU, friend, since I'm a cookie stamper with a mustache.
Remember James's farmer, waiting on the rain? Elijah prays earnestly, and his prayer is all about the weather.

cards.question: What did Elijah pray earnestly for?

answers.text: That the sun would stand still

cards.question: After Elijah prayed, how long did it not rain on the land?

cards.text: Three and a half YEARS, friend, and I fuss when my oven takes ten extra minutes. Then Elijah prays again.

cards.question: After Elijah's second prayer, James says the heavens give ___, and the earth yields its ___.

cards.text: James has one more thing for the brothers. What if one of them wanders from the truth, and someone brings him back?

cards.question: James says whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will do what?

answers.text: Earn a place among the elders

cards.text: And he'll cover over a multitude of sins. That's where James ends his whole letter, friend, with one brother bringing another one back.

findings.problem: The parenthetical reference Job 1:13-19 names Job immediately before card 12 asks which man's perseverance James mentions. It therefore gives away the next card's answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card retells the farmer waiting for rain from James 5:7, but its citation is only James 5:17. The citation does not cover all the passage material the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says Elijah's prayer is all about the weather. Of card 12's answers, only that it would not rain concerns weather; the sun standing still and the sea parting do not. The setup therefore rules out both wrong answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The stops repeat essentially the same question-type pattern. In both stops, the first nine choice cards run multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice, multiple choice, fill in the blank. The repeated opening cycle is also formulaic in itself.

rule.text: They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
